subject: Physics
scope: Seven original AQA AS/A-level Physics refraction/optical-fibre single-fact mock-recall cards; step-index fibres only.
notes: Focused additions to the v159 45-point Waves mock audit, not a replacement. AQA 3.3.2.3 lists cladding, TIR, material/modal dispersion and pulse broadening. Additional cladding protection and crosstalk are explanatory applications rather than separate quoted specification bullets. No complete full-specification certification.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Why is protective cladding useful even though total internal reflection guides light in the core?
cards.back: It protects the core from scratches or damage that could cause light loss.
accept: It protects the core from scratches or damage that could cause light loss.
The cladding protects the core from damage and reduces light loss.
It prevents damage to the core surface that might let light escape.
Cladding stops scratches disrupting total internal reflection.
reject: It increases the refractive index of the core.
It causes the light to be absorbed intentionally.
It allows total internal reflection even if light enters from the lower-index medium.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: How does cladding help stop signals in neighbouring optical fibres interfering?
cards.back: It limits light leakage between neighbouring fibre cores (optical crosstalk).
accept: It limits light leakage between neighbouring fibre cores (optical crosstalk).
The cladding reduces light crossing into adjacent fibres.
It prevents optical crosstalk between neighbouring fibre cores.
It helps confine light so it does not enter another fibre.
reject: The cladding sends the optical signal into neighbouring fibres.
It causes the light pulses in every fibre to overlap.
It makes the light travel faster than in a vacuum.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: At the critical angle, what direction does the refracted ray take?
cards.back: It travels along the boundary, at 90° to the normal.
accept: It travels along the boundary, at 90° to the normal.
The refracted ray is at 90 degrees to the normal.
It runs along the interface.
The angle of refraction is 90°.
reject: The ray is totally internally reflected at any angle.
The refracted angle is zero degrees.
The ray bends towards the normal.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What two conditions must be met for total internal reflection at a boundary?
cards.back: Light must go from higher to lower refractive index, with incidence angle greater than the critical angle.
accept: Light must go from higher to lower refractive index, with incidence angle greater than the critical angle.
From the higher-index medium to the lower-index medium at an angle above the critical angle.
The first refractive index must be higher, and the incident angle exceeds the critical angle.
Light must strike from the optically denser side at an angle larger than the critical angle.
reject: Total internal reflection occurs from lower to higher refractive index.
Any incidence angle below the critical angle causes total internal reflection.
The angle must equal the critical angle for total internal reflection.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What change to the light source reduces material dispersion in a step-index fibre?
cards.back: Use light with a narrower range of wavelengths (approximately monochromatic light).
accept: Use light with a narrower range of wavelengths (approximately monochromatic light).
Use monochromatic light to reduce material dispersion.
Reduce the spread of wavelengths in the light source.
Choose a source emitting a very narrow wavelength range.
reject: Use a wider range of wavelengths.
Use a higher absorption fibre.
Increase the number of different wavelengths in each pulse.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What design change can reduce modal dispersion in a step-index optical fibre?
cards.back: Use a narrower core that supports fewer modes (light paths).
accept: Use a narrower core that supports fewer modes (light paths).
Reduce the core width so fewer modes propagate.
A thin core reduces the number of ray paths and modal dispersion.
Use a sufficiently narrow core to allow fewer modes.
reject: Increase the number of ray paths.
Use a broader range of wavelengths to reduce modal dispersion.
Make the core wide so light has more different path lengths.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is the difference between absorption and dispersion in an optical fibre?
cards.back: Absorption reduces signal intensity; dispersion spreads a light pulse in time.
accept: Absorption reduces signal intensity; dispersion spreads a light pulse in time.
Absorption weakens the pulse, while dispersion broadens it.
Absorption lowers power and dispersion increases pulse duration.
Absorption removes signal energy whereas dispersion causes pulses to spread.
reject: Absorption spreads the pulse in time while dispersion removes all light energy.
Both processes only change the light's frequency.
Dispersion alone always destroys all the signal energy.
